evidence_snippet: Both products are computed in int32, so for large `batch x vocab_size` tensors the offsets can silently overflow, corrupting loads/stores.
rationale: Large batch-vocab flattened offsets overflowed int32 in the Triton renorm kernels, corrupting memory accesses. Casting to int64 fixes the large-shape edge.
counterfactual_rationale: A sampling-kernel test with large batch-vocab products near int32 overflow would expose the corruption; memcheck could also flag bad accesses.

affected_hardware: CUDA EP deployments using NIXL all-to-all
evidence_snippet: `nixl-ep` cannot be used as an all2all backend unless elastic EP is also enabled
rationale: NIXL EP all-to-all asserted on a missing tcp_store_group in the standard EP path, unintentionally coupling it to elastic EP. The fix constructs a stateless group from the CPU group.
counterfactual_rationale: Launching a standard expert-parallel serving job with the nixl_ep backend and without elastic EP would have caught the assertion.

evidence_snippet: torch.topk with sorted=False ... the returned experts aren't necessarily in score order

counterfactual_rationale: Randomized top-k score tests that assert the shared expert replaces the minimum score, or an equivalence proof of the selection logic, would detect this.

evidence_snippet: forward_xpu could pass float32 cos_sin_cache with bfloat16 Q/K, triggering RuntimeError: expected scalar type BFloat16 but found Float.

counterfactual_rationale: An XPU CI lane covering multimodal MRoPE with bf16 Q/K would have exercised this dtype mismatch.

evidence_snippet: produces an integer overflow resulting in negative offsets which result in a GPU segfault
